source.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Antibody Language Models Using SAEs
source.authors: Rebonto Haque; Oliver M. Turnbull; Anisha Parsan; Nithin Parsan; John J. Yang; Anna L. Beukenhorst; Charlotte M. Deane

record.tranche_reason: The study qualitatively compares hidden-neuron activation patterns with SAE-latent patterns for a concept in an antibody language model; it does not use the original vision-model analysis.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a visual comparison of neuron and latent activations for CDRH3. Its claim that scattered neuron activations may reflect polysemanticity is tentative; it does not count polysemantic neurons or test their responses across unrelated token or context sets. The probe accuracies and SAE steering results do not measure neuron polysemanticity and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study assumes polysemanticity from superposition as the motivation for SAEs. Its only neuron evidence is one qualitative plot, used as a baseline against its own SAE latents. It shows top-correlated hidden-unit activations scattered over one test antibody (Figure 1a). The authors offer polysemanticity only as a possible explanation ("may be explained by"). They do not measure whether units respond to unrelated inputs, how common this is, or how it varies by layer. The units are hidden-layer (residual) activations, not MLP neurons. So the study reports its own method's interpretability rather than a rate or strength of neuron polysemanticity.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right; the main conclusion is about SAEs, not neurons. TopK SAEs reveal biologically meaningful latents (CDR identity, J-gene identity), but high latent–concept correlation does not guarantee causal control over generation. Ordered SAEs reliably yield steerable features, at the cost of less interpretable activation patterns. These patterns replicate on IgLM and ProGen2-OAS. Neuron polysemanticity is mentioned only as a possible reason neuron activations look scattered.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a visual comparison of neuron and SAE-latent activation patterns in antibody language models rather than reproducing the original source's analysis.

fits_no_version.finding: In p-IgGen layer 3, top CDRH3-correlated hidden-unit activations are scattered across one test antibody, while SAE latents localise to CDRH3 (Figure 1a). The authors speculate this reflects polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hidden-layer (residual) units in small protein/antibody language models are less position-specific for biological concepts than SAE latents (qualitative, single example).

record.problems: The neuron evidence is qualitative and limited to a displayed test-antibody sequence; the paper does not quantify neuron prevalence or establish that the scattered activations correspond to unrelated features.
record.rows_left_out: The neuron-versus-latent CDRH3 probe accuracies are not rows because prediction accuracy does not measure polysemanticity. Other SAE feature-prediction and steering results concern SAE latents or generated sequences, not neuron polysemanticity.

untested.parts: Share of polysemantic MLP neurons, responses to unrelated tokens or contexts, and layer differences: none are measured.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T2 to uses_without_test/T4. Polysemanticity appears as background (Section 2.2) and as a speculative explanation of one qualitative figure. The 'hidden neuron' activations are hidden-layer outputs that the SAEs were trained on, not MLP neurons. The neuron probe accuracy (0.98 vs 0.99 for latents) concerns information content, not polysemanticity.

versions.untested_parts: No image classifier or vision-model neurons are studied.

The study does not quantify the share of polysemantic neurons, specify that the neurons are MLP neurons, systematically compare layers, or test responses across unrelated token or context sets. Its evidence is a qualitative activation visualization for CDRH3.
The study gives no test of feature capacity pressure or whether more features than neurons are represented.
The study does not test polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.

The study compares SAE types and antibody-model architectures for latent identification and steering, not how architecture or training changes the share of polysemantic neurons or its performance cost.
The study does not determine whether apparently mixed neuron activations correspond to a shared feature or related jobs.
The study does not vary activation range or explanation-scoring method to assess how polysemanticity classification changes.

rows.subject: p-IgGen
rows.operation_detail: Visually compared hidden-neuron activations with SAE-latent activations for CDRH3 identity.
rows.measure: Qualitative activation pattern across sequence positions
rows.value: Hidden-neuron activations were described as scattered across the sequence with no discernible pattern; the authors say this may reflect multiple features associated with unrelated residues being represented by one neuron.
rows.note: The comparison also shows localized SAE-latent activation for CDRH3, but the row records only the neuron result. The authors present polysemanticity as a possible explanation, not a direct demonstration that the activations correspond to unrelated inputs.
rows.check: This is the study's method (SAE latents) compared against a neuron baseline, shown in one qualitative plot for one test sequence. The units are hidden-layer activations, not MLP neurons. A scattered activation pattern does not show responses to unrelated tokens or contexts, and the authors only hypothesise polysemanticity. The measure cannot show V2's effect. The 'partial' state is unsupported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The neuron pattern is described as scattered, but this is a single qualitative visualization and does not establish unrelated token or context responses or how common the pattern is (r1).
